newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply down after heavy liquidatio.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply down after heavy liquidatio.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures slumped on Monday after a turnaround in NYMEX heating oil's fortunes triggered technical selling stops across the oil complex and the liquidation of positions by local traders and large investment funds alike, brokers said.
Feb Brent closed a hefty 86 cents down at $23.50 a barrel, just three cents off the session low, having crashed through trendline support at $24.18.
"It was a combination of a lot of (technical) stops being set off and the large funds moving out," said one broker.
Having opened strongly on forecasts of colder weather in the U.S. Northwest, NYMEX heating oil performed a startling U-turn shedding nearly three cents a gallon on the day.
Feb NYMEX crude failed to hold key support at $26 and $25.40 a barrel.
"The market has been overbought for a long time and needed a shakeout," said one broker.
"There was a lot of stale length in London and it's being liquidated."

Expectations of colder weather in the U.S. Northeast, the world's key heating oil region, were undermined by predictions of warmer temperatures by some regional forecasters, said U.S. market watchers.
In Europe, temperatures were already milder after a long cold snap.
Feb gas oil also fell heavily to close earlier at $219 a tonne, down $7.25. The Feb/Mar backwardation shed $2 over the session to close at $8.25 a tonne.
The Feb Brent/gas oil crack spread ended the day at $5.41 a barrel.
